scope: Independent native lifecycle implementation comparison; actual KVM lifecycle gate pending

sources.observation: Expiration metadata persists the original expires_at separately from in-memory timer tracking.
Per-sandbox lifecycle locks serialize expiration. The tracked deadline can be recovered from persistence; cleanup retries reschedule without changing the original tracked expiration.
A flock lease belongs to an open file description and survives fork until the duplicate descriptors close.
Forked children inherit their process cgroup. Later process migration does not migrate children that already exist.

application: Persist the original UTC absolute deadline with host boot ID and CLOCK_BOOTTIME deadline; reconnect never renews the budget.
Use per-sandbox locks for native operations and a short independent installation admission lock. Do not serialize all VM startup/RPC work behind one long-lived lock.
Run a separate authenticated Rust supervisor so TTL and VMM console draining survive caller death. OpenSandbox timer code alone does not establish this independent-process guarantee.
Join each task-owned supervisor/VMM cgroup in pre_exec before exec; the inherited CLOEXEC installation lease fences caller-death recovery until helper placement.
Require actual process/namespace/cgroup/artifact identity before signaling and positive physical absence before reporting collection.
not_accepted: actual new native lifecycle hardware behavior
